subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: Core pivot (strip autonomous feature scoring; make bug priority agent-driven with context-only question tool) is sound and boring in the right way: removes a noisy autonomous-write surface and collapses a dual-mode command to single-mode. The 'question tool for context only, never to confirm priority' distinction is well-modeled and consistent across AC4/DONT8. The max-2-questions-then-default-medium budget with a context_insufficient flag is a reasonable bounded-autonomy guardrail; no race risk because Phase 4c operates on a single triage run reading `gh issue list --state open` and skips already-labeled issues (idempotent-resume mitigation explicit). AC6 nullable-field retention verified feasible against roadmap.ts (wsjf number|null; null-tolerant sort). Removed-phases table cleanly maps AC1/AC2/AC3/AC5. HOWEVER two contract items are inadequately covered and one is a spec-as-laws contradiction. (1) rq-backlogCoord09 still legislates 'Bug Priority remains user-owned' in three locations; the design's spec-delta only deletes rq06 and vaguely says 'update 01-05,07-09', never identifying that rq09 must be rewritten. Left unfixed, this ships a spec law the new command violates. (2) AC11 requires updating backlog.ts WSJF comments (its line-13 comment cites rq-backlogCoord06 which AC9 deletes -> dangling reference), yet design + proposal both list backlog.ts under 'Files kept unchanged.' A comment-only edit does not violate C1 (read-only, no code/write-path removal), but the design must reconcile this and add backlog.ts to its modification surface. Minor: spec-delta overstates edit surface (reqs 01-04,07 contain no scoring references; only 05.1 incidental WSJF-staleness and rq09 actually reference it). CLARIFY_MISSING_ERROR_HANDLING (partial GH label-apply failure mid-loop) unaddressed.

blockers: rq-backlogCoord09 contradiction (spec-as-laws): rq-backlogCoord09 asserts 'Bug Priority and feature Value remain user-owned' in body (line 370), scenario 09.1 (line 383 'before any bug Priority prompt'), and scenario 09.4 (line 422). This directly contradicts AC5 (remove user-only guardrail) and DONT7 (do not re-introduce bug-priority-is-user-only). The design's spec-delta only deletes rq-backlogCoord06 and vaguely says 'update rq-backlogCoord01-05,07-09'; it never identifies rq09's user-owned-bug-priority invariant as needing rewrite. Design MUST explicitly specify the rq-backlogCoord09 rewrite: decouple bug-Priority from the user-owned model while keeping feature-Value user-owned (features are out of the agent-driven pivot) and preserving cleanup-before-prompt ordering.

AC11 has no design coverage and contradicts 'Files kept unchanged': AC11 requires updating backlog.ts WSJF-related comments. backlog.ts header comment (lines 13-16) cites 'rq-backlogCoord06' which AC9 deletes (dangling spec reference) and describes stripped Value(V) scoring semantics. Both design and proposal list backlog.ts under 'Files kept unchanged.' The design must add backlog.ts (comment-only edits) to its modification surface and clarify comment-only edits still respect C1 (no code/write-path removal). As written, the design is self-contradictory on this point.
validation.notes: Both blockers are contract-coverage/spec-consistency defects, not implementation-impossibility — fixable via a design amendment; neither invalidates the core architecture. Non-blocking cautions: (a) AC13 no-regression is implicit only — add an explicit verification task; (b) spec-delta overstates edit surface — narrow to purpose + rq06 delete + rq09 rewrite + rq05.1 incidental wording; (c) design does not specify behavior when a `gh` label-apply fails mid-loop (partial-application/rollback/resume) — add a mitigation row; (d) confirm rq-backlogCoord06.2's `.adv/github-project.json` field-set reference is reconciled with AC8 GH Project field drop so no other req dangles.

tradeoffs: Agent-driven bug priority trades user-per-issue control for throughput; bounded by max-2-question budget + default-medium fallback, so overreach risk is capped but non-zero (agent may mislabel low-context bugs as medium).

Keeping nullable RoadmapFeature wsjf/rroe/effort/value/time_criticality fields preserves backward-compat with the existing snapshot and avoids a data migration (DONT3), at the cost of retaining dead-ish schema surface until GH Project fields are dropped — an acceptable, reversible debt.

Deleting rq-backlogCoord06 while rewriting rq-backlogCoord09 is a larger spec edit than the design scoped; doing it correctly is necessary to avoid spec/impl drift and stays inside the capability (does not touch DONT5 Epic / DONT6 backlog).

Rationale-trailer `<bug>: priority=<tier> :: <rationale>` in chat run-summary (not issue comments) is structurally sound and avoids leaking agent rationale to PR-visible surfaces; trade-off is rationale is ephemeral (not persisted to the issue), the correct call to avoid comment noise.

# Proposal: Scope `/adv-triage` to bugs/issues only

## Problem

`/adv-triage` currently handles two unrelated workflows in one command:
- **Bug triage**: `priority:{critical,high,medium,low}` labels on GH issues — currently **user-only**
- **Feature scoring**: WSJF (Value + TimeCriticality + RROE) / Effort on GH Project v2 number fields, then regen `ROADMAP.md` — autonomous

Both modes are problematic:
- Autonomous feature scoring writes are noisy, scores go stale, GH Project UI is authoritative anyway.
- User-only bug priority forces every issue through the user, even when context is obvious.

The user wants a cleaner model: triage becomes a **bugs-only** command with **agent-driven priority assignment** (autonomous, with user questions to gather triage context — never to confirm priority).

## Approach

### Feature side (strip)

Strip autonomous feature scoring and field-write paths. Remove:
- Phase 5 (Agent Scoring) — autonomous V/TC/RROE/Effort assignment
- All GH Project number-field writes (`Value`, `TimeCriticality`, `RROE`, `Effort`, `WSJF` fields dropped from GH Project)
- `--rescore` flag
- WSJF.md Agent scoring + GraphQL writes sections
- All `gh api graphql` mutation rows from `Key Tools` table
- ROADMAP.md V/TC/RROE/E/WSJF columns

### Bug side (pivot to agent-driven)

Reframe Phase 4c:
- Agent analyzes each open bug using body, comments, recent activity, linked PRs, related issues.
- Agent applies `priority:{critical,high,medium,low}` label autonomously based on analysis.
- Agent uses `question` tool to gather **context** when needed (e.g., "is this regression in production?"), NOT to confirm priority choice.
- Agent emits a brief rationale trailer per priority assignment.

# Design: Scope /adv-triage to bugs only

## Architecture

`/adv-triage` becomes a **bugs-only** command with **agent-driven priority assignment**. Two semantic shifts:

### Shift 1 — Strip autonomous feature scoring

Removed phases/sections:
- Phase 5 (Agent Scoring) — gone
- `--rescore` flag — gone
- `gh api graphql` mutation rows in Key Tools — gone
- WSJF.md Agent scoring + GraphQL writes + Idempotent resume + Evidence block sections — gone
- `× MUST NOT autofill bug priority — user-only` guardrail — flipped

### Shift 2 — Pivot bug priority to agent-driven (idempotent, partial-apply safe)

**Loop:**
1. Read open bugs (`gh issue list --state open --label bug`).
2. For each bug, fetch existing `priority:*` label; skip if already set (idempotency).
3. Agent analyzes body, comments, recent activity, linked PRs/issues.
4. Agent derives a priority tier with brief rationale.
5. If context ambiguous, agent uses `question` tool to gather ONE clarification (e.g., "is this regression in production?"). **Never** to confirm priority choice. Budget: max 2 calls per bug.
6. Agent emits `<issue#>: priority=<tier> :: <rationale>` trailer.
7. Apply label via `gh issue edit --add-label priority:{tier}`.
8. On label-apply failure (network/auth/etc.): log error, continue to next bug.
9. Default `medium` + `context_insufficient` flag if question budget exhausted.

Final report: successes, failures, skipped (already-labeled, context_insufficient). Re-running resumes from unlabeled bugs.

**Rationale trailer surface:** chat output (triage run summary) only — NEVER issue comments (avoid leaking to PR-visible surfaces).

## Implementation strategy

### Files modified

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `.opencode/command/adv-triage.md` | Remove Phase 5; remove `--rescore`; remove GraphQL mutation rows; reframe Phase 4c as agent-driven priority loop (Loop spec above); update H1 + description |
| `plugin/src/skills/adv-triage/SKILL.md` | Drop `wsjf, scoring` from keywords; drop step 7; remove Quick Formulas; remove scoring-only anti-patterns |
| `plugin/src/skills/adv-triage/WSJF.md` | Keep Match algorithm; strip Agent scoring, GraphQL writes, Idempotent resume, Evidence block sections |
| `plugin/src/skills/adv-triage/SCHEMA.md` | Drop V/TC/RROE/E/WSJF columns from ROADMAP.md feature table; sort rule (issue#-asc fallback when all WSJF null) |
| `plugin/src/skills/adv-triage/PROMPTS.md` | Remove `Autofill all features`; remove Feature Value options; restrict prompts to bug-priority context-gathering |
| `plugin/src/skills/adv-triage/BOOTSTRAP.md` | Drop Value/TC/RROE/Effort/WSJF from required custom fields table |
| `plugin/src/skills/adv-triage/ANTI-PATTERNS.md` | Remove scoring-only anti-patterns (--rescore abuse, GraphQL mutation cadence) |
| `plugin/src/tools/backlog.ts` | **COMMENT-ONLY edit** — header L13-16 references `rq-backlogCoord06` (deleted) and describes stripped Value semantics. Update to "all scoring fields may be null; tool is read-only on snapshot". **No code changes** (still respects C1: tool layer is read-only) |
| `bin/adv` | Drop `--rescore`; drop WSJF-column help text |
| `.adv/specs/backlog-coordination/spec.json` | Delete `rq-backlogCoord06` (+ 06.1, 06.2); **REWRITE** `rq-backlogCoord09` body + scenarios 09.1, 09.4 (currently assert user-only bug priority); update capability `purpose` |

### Files kept unchanged (truly read-only)

- `plugin/src/tools/roadmap.ts` (read paths; nullable fields stay)
- `bin/lib/roadmap.ts` (read-only)
- `roadmap-origin-sanitize.ts` (protective)

### Operator action (post-archive)

Drop `Value`, `TimeCriticality`, `RROE`, `Effort`, `WSJF` custom fields from GH Project (via UI or `gh project field-delete`). Documented in archive notes.

## Spec deltas (rq- prefix changes)

- **Delete:** `rq-backlogCoord06`, `rq-backlogCoord06.1`, `rq-backlogCoord06.2` (autonomous TC/RROE/E clauses; agent owns priority now)
- **Rewrite:** `rq-backlogCoord09` body (L370) + scenarios 09.1 (L383) + 09.4 (L422) — currently assert "user-only bug priority"; rewrite to "agent-driven priority with bounded-autonomous rationale (max 2 question-budget per bug, default `medium` + `context_insufficient`); user questions gather context only — never confirm priority"
- **Keep unchanged:** `rq-backlogCoord01-04`, `rq-backlogCoord05`, `rq-backlogCoord07-08` (claim infra, WIP, freshness)
- **Update:** capability `purpose` — drop "GitHub Project remains canonical for ranking and Value (V)"
- **Add (implicit, no rq- id needed):** Phase 4c agent-driven priority loop; documented in prose + tests

## Test strategy

- **New:** `adv-triage-phase4c-agent.test.ts` — agent-driven loop: labels applied, rationale trailer present, `question` tool used for context only (never priority confirmation), 2-question budget respected, idempotent re-run skips already-labeled bugs, partial-apply failure handling, rationale trailer goes to chat only (not issue comments)
- **New:** `roadmap-render-no-scoring-cols.test.ts` — ROADMAP.md drops V/TC/RROE/E/WSJF columns
- **New:** `rq-backlogCoord09-spec-compliance.test.ts` — verify rewritten spec body + scenarios match agent-driven model
- **Update:** tests asserting Phase 5 / GraphQL mutation presence — delete or rewrite
- **Keep:** `adv_backlog_state` read-path tests; `sortFeaturesByWsjf` tests (nullable fallback)

## CI gate (AC13 — explicit)

- `pnpm run check` green: schemas:check, typecheck, lint, format:check, lockfile policy, test-isolation, full test suite
- No regression in `adv-triage-relevance-assets.test.ts` (delete assertions referencing removed Phase 5)
- No regression in `checkpoint-surface-drift.test.ts` (Phase 5.2 reference)

## Local-first best practices

- **Comment-only edit on read-only tool layer** (backlog.ts). Code unchanged. Tool-layer read-only invariant preserved (C1).
- **Campsite rule**: leave spec + skills cleaner than found.
- **No silent behavior change** — every removed feature documented in proposal + agreement + AC list.

## Architectural risks

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Agent over-applies priority without enough context | Per-bug budget (max 2 questions); default `medium` + `context_insufficient` flag |
| ROADMAP.md regression (existing autoscored features lose data) | Keep nullable fields in `RoadmapFeature` type |
| GH Project field deletion is operator-dependent | Document in archive notes; pre-archive check |
| Phase 4c agent loop stateful — needs idempotent resume | Skip already-labeled bugs; re-run safe |
| Rationale trailer leaks to GH comments | Trailer goes in chat output, NEVER issue comments |
| Partial label-apply (some bugs labeled, others fail) | Log + continue; final report surfaces failures |
